text:
Minnesota arrives at Seattle on game three of a five-game road trip, 0-1-1 so far, after a 2-1 loss at CGY two days ago. The Wild are 2-2-1 in their last five and are missing Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno, though Maxim Shabanov is day-to-day and could return. Seattle beat UTA 5-3 and is 3-1-1 in its last five, without Jared McCann, who is out until about Oct. 28. Berkly Catton is next in line for his minutes, and Bobby McMann is the likeliest to move up on the power play.

The Wild have driven the play: 54% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) at five on five, against 45% for the Kraken. Seattle's +5 goal difference sits on -4.7 expected, with finishing doing the lifting. Minnesota also holds a power-play edge, 0.84 expected goals per game to 0.63. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt is +6.8 goals saved above expected this season, while Seattle's projected Joey Daccord is at -2.3, after -6.1 last season.

Kirill Kaprizov is 52% to score. As Heather Rule of NHL.com posted, Quinn Hughes has 11 assists in 10 games and Kaprizov 11 goals in 10. Hughes is two points from 500 career points. Our under-the-radar pick is Joel Eriksson Ek, 59% for a point, above his season pace of 50%, with his line creating chances. For Seattle, Jordan Eberle leads the group at 25% to score.
